title: Deep rock grain, graded down with depth
question: Does one of these read as rock rather than television static — or are they close enough that this change is not worth having?
context_md:
You ruled 'just make the change' on grading the per-pixel grain down at depth, on my claim that `JITTER_STRENGTH 0.12` was the loudest thing in every cave render. **The change is real but my claim was wrong, and the numbers are why I want your eye on it rather than my word.**

Grain now fades from full strength at the skyline to a third of it over the same 64-row ramp the depth light uses — the same pure function of (x, y, horizon[x]), so the dirty-rect skip is untouched.

**What I measured after.** Setting the floor to *zero* — grain entirely off at depth — barely moved the picture, which is how I caught the wrong attribution. Apportioned with mean-absolute-deviation from the 3x3 neighbourhood mean (so smooth gradients score ~0):

| | luma MAD | chroma MAD |
|---|---|---|
| current | 3.017 | 1.374 |
| graded to 1/3 (pane B) | 2.325 | — |
| grain OFF entirely | 2.090 | 1.301 |

So this change removes **23% of the luma speckle and almost none of the chroma**. The rest is `palette_family` drawing a *per-cell* coin flip between neutral grey and warm sandstone — ~40 brightness points and a big hue shift apart, pixel by pixel. That is open bug 0b, it is in `passes.rs` where round 5 is live, and it is scheduled for round 6.

**So the honest question is whether a 23% cut is visible at all to you**, given the bigger cause is still in. If these two panes look the same, say so — I would rather revert it than carry a change that buys nothing.
